# Agent Orchestrator

A VS Code extension that turns one request into a plan and runs it across the coding CLIs the
author already pays for. An [[openrouter]] model reads the workspace, decides whether the request
needs one answer or several agents, splits it into a DAG of subtasks, routes each to
[[claude-code-cli]] or [[codex-cli]] at a chosen model and reasoning effort, runs independent work
in parallel ([[dag-scheduling-in-waves]]), and merges the results.

The repository folder is `vs-llm-orchestrator`; the product inside it is
`agent-orchestrator`. One repository holds both, for reasons recorded in
[[one-repository-at-the-workspace-folder]].

## Shape

| Part | Language | Lines | Responsibility |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `backend/graph.py` | Python + [[langgraph]] | 5,332 | reconnaissance, planning, scheduling, CLI execution, fallback, merge, durable goals, and the stdio protocol |
| `extension/src/extension.ts` | TypeScript, [[vs-code-extension-api]] | 895 | backend lifecycle, SecretStorage, configuration, event fan-out, and replay recording |
| `extension/media/panel.html` | one file | 2,815 | markup, CSS, and the event reducer for both surfaces -- [[self-contained-single-file-html]] |
| `skills/` | markdown | 30 skills | vendored playbooks granted per session, installed nowhere |

Three processes share one machine. Nothing is hosted and no component listens on a socket. The
extension has zero runtime dependencies and the webview has no build step
([[zero-dependency-no-build-step]]).

## The split

LangGraph is Python and the extension API is TypeScript, so the graph runs as a subprocess. That
leaves the graph runnable and testable without VS Code, while the extension spawns it, forwards
events, and renders them. One JSON object per line in each direction is the complete protocol,
which is what makes [[replay-a-recorded-run]] possible.

## Durable goals and portable replay

Each request belongs to a durable goal. **Send** continues the active goal; **New goal** explicitly
starts a replacement. Acceptance criteria and verified evidence survive a backend restart or panel
reload, so a reader can distinguish a continuing task from a new one.

Large input is staged in chunks before planning. Input, prompts, provider events, tool events, and
results enter a redacted durable trace before the equivalent live event is forwarded. The panel loads
retained trace records on demand and preserves which details the reader expanded. The recorded
`dag-waves` fixture keeps a real run's event order while using portable paths:
`/workspace/dag-waves/scratchpad/ws5`, `/usr/local/bin/claude`, and
`/usr/local/bin/codex`.

## Autonomy

Both CLIs run non-interactively, so the autonomy level is chosen before the run and passed as flags
([[autonomy-decided-before-the-run]]). `readonly` maps to plan/read-only modes; `auto` maps to
accept-edits/workspace-write with a build, test, and inspect allow-list; and `full` maps to
bypass-permissions/danger-full-access. Since 0.10.0, `full` is the shipped default. It is stated
plainly as a choice, not presented as a sandbox.

The router is the only component that sees every subtask output and has no tools. A prompt can
persuade it to produce a wrong answer, but cannot directly produce an action.

## Verification

The 2026-08-12 local audit passed 345 backend tests, 44 recorded-run panel checks, TypeScript
compilation, and 25 repository guards. Extension-host coverage has 33 checks for both source and
installed builds. The sandbox could not read the owner's default pytest temporary directory, so that
audit supplied an external writable temporary root; that is an execution-host limit, not a product
failure. The real CLIs, OpenRouter API, and live permission behaviour were not exercised by this
non-display audit.

## Status

Version 0.10.0 is working and not published. Marketplace publication remains blocked by a rotated-key
requirement, placeholder publisher metadata, no repository field or Marketplace PNG icon, and no
Marketplace screenshots until a repository URL exists. `docs/RELEASING.md` section 3 is the current
checklist.

## Git and documentation

The product was imported into Git at `vs-llm-orchestrator/` on 2026-08-08 after existing as a
folder. At that point, `brain.py verify-sources` changed from reporting it as not a Git repository
to reporting it clean; source cleanliness is now checked separately for each audit.

The repository has an ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 requirements specification (162 functional and 8
non-functional requirements), architecture and security documents, a test plan, risk register,
release procedure, and 19 ADRs. The 60-plus-image screenshot matrix is generated from recorded runs,
so a figure is a repeatable visual check rather than an illustrative mockup
([[readme-as-guided-tour]]).

The 30 vendored skills retain their upstream URL, license, and exact commit in a `NOTICE` file:
[[agent-skills-checked-into-the-repo]] and [[provenance-notice-file]].
